"Genre: 3D Soulslike Action RPG / Dark Fantasy / Open-World Exploration
Perspective: Third-person
Visual Style: High-quality 3D dark fantasy with whimsical fairytale environments
Combat Inspiration: Dark Souls, Elden Ring, Lies of P
Platform: PC (controller and keyboard support)
1. GAME OVERVIEW
Create a fully playable third-person 3D Soulslike action RPG titled THE HOLLOW CROWN.
The player is an ordinary modern-day human who is mysteriously transported from 2026 into a whimsical medieval fantasy kingdom called Eldoria.
The kingdom initially appears colorful, magical, and fairytale-like, filled with enchanted forests, talking creatures, enormous mushrooms, medieval villages, castles, and magical landscapes.
However, a terrible corruption has spread throughout the kingdom. Villagers have transformed into hostile creatures, knights have become undead monsters, and ancient supernatural entities are awakening.
The player's ultimate objective is to fight through six interconnected regions, defeat powerful bosses, uncover the kingdom's secrets, and confront an ancient eldritch wizard responsible for bringing them into this world.
Eventually, the player must face an enormous unholy demon threatening to consume all of existence.
2. PLAYER CHARACTER
Create a customizable human protagonist.
The character begins wearing recognizable modern clothing, including a hoodie, pants, and sneakers.
Starting equipment:
Broken smartphone (nonfunctional).
Improvised metal pipe.
Basic healing item.
No armor.
No magical abilities.
The character must gradually evolve from an ordinary human into a powerful warrior.
Implement:
Character movement.
Sprinting.
Jumping.
Dodging and rolling.
Lock-on targeting.
Light and heavy attacks.
Blocking and parrying.
Stamina management.
Health management.
Weapon switching.
Armor equipment.
Healing animations.
Death and respawn mechanics.
Include character progression through experience, currency, attributes, weapons, armor, and magical abilities.
3. CORE COMBAT SYSTEM
Implement challenging Soulslike combat.
Combat must be deliberate and weighty rather than fast-paced hack-and-slash.
Every weapon should have unique attack animations, damage values, stamina consumption, and attack ranges.
Weapon categories:
Straight swords.
Greatswords.
Daggers.
Axes.
Warhammers.
Spears.
Bows.
Magical staffs.
Unique boss weapons.
Combat mechanics:
Enemy telegraph animations.
Perfect dodge timing.
Parrying and critical attacks.
Stagger and poise systems.
Backstab attacks.
Critical finishing animations.
Boss health bars.
Multiple boss phases.
Environmental hazards.
Enemies must be dangerous enough that careless attacks can result in death.
4. WORLD DESIGN
Create six interconnected explorable regions with interconnected paths, shortcuts, hidden rooms, treasure, dungeons, NPCs, and boss arenas.
REGION 1: THE FORGOTTEN SHIRE
A whimsical medieval countryside filled with abandoned cottages, colorful flowers, enchanted hills, and corrupted villagers.
Enemies:
Infected villagers.
Glimmer goblins.
Hollow woodland creatures.
Rotten knights.
Main Boss: THE HOLLOW WOODSMAN.
A gigantic lumberjack with a massive axe and a tree growing through his chest.
REGION 2: THE WEEPING WILDS
A magical forest with enormous mushrooms, glowing plants, twisted trees, and underground fungal caverns.
Enemies:
Giant spiders.
Infected animals.
Mushroom creatures.
Root monsters.
Main Boss: MOTHER MYCELIA.
A grotesque mushroom queen who controls the forest through fungal roots.
REGION 3: THE KINGDOM OF ASHENVEIL
A sprawling medieval city with gothic cathedrals, burning streets, ruined marketplaces, and enormous castles.
Enemies:
Undead knights.
Executioners.
Plague doctors.
Corrupted royal guards.
Main Boss: KING ALDRIC, THE UNCROWNED.
A gigantic armored king wielding an enormous cursed sword.
REGION 4: THE FROSTBITTEN REACH
A frozen mountain kingdom containing abandoned fortresses, frozen lakes, ancient tombs, and blizzards.
Enemies:
Frozen warriors.
Ice giants.
Undead wolves.
Frost wraiths.
Main Boss: THE PALE SAINT.
A horrifying winged executioner inside a frozen cathedral.
REGION 5: THE SHATTERED HEAVENS
A surreal cosmic environment containing floating islands, broken castles, upside-down architecture, and strange celestial creatures.
Enemies:
Voidborn.
Floating aberrations.
Cosmic knights.
Distorted humanoids.
Main Boss: THE STARVED ORACLE.
A many-eyed celestial creature capable of manipulating gravity and creating illusions.
REGION 6: THE BLACK SPIRE
An enormous eldritch tower stretching into the heavens, surrounded by a seemingly endless void.
Enemies:
Malgraven's experiments.
Failed dimensional travelers.
Eldritch abominations.
Ancient corrupted guardians.
Main Boss: MALGRAVEN, THE LAST SEER.
The ancient wizard responsible for summoning the protagonist.
5. ENEMY AI
Create intelligent enemy behavior.
Enemies must:
Patrol designated areas.
Detect the player through vision and proximity.
Investigate suspicious sounds.
Pursue the player.
Attack using different patterns.
Retreat or reposition when appropriate.
Coordinate attacks in groups.
Return to patrol if the player escapes.
Each enemy type must have unique animations, movement, sounds, attack patterns, and visual designs.
Include rare elite enemies and hidden mini-boss encounters.
6. BOSS DESIGN
Every major boss must have:
Unique 3D character models.
Custom animations.
Distinctive music.
A dedicated arena.
Multiple combat phases.
Unique attack patterns.
Environmental interactions.
A cinematic introduction.
A dramatic death animation.
Unique rewards.
Boss difficulty should progressively increase throughout the campaign.
Bosses must not feel like oversized ordinary enemies. They should have recognizable personalities and memorable combat mechanics.
7. NPC AND QUEST SYSTEM
Populate Eldoria with survivors, merchants, mysterious travelers, talking creatures, and strange magical beings.
Create branching dialogue and questlines.
NPCs should remember important player decisions.
Some NPCs can:
Sell equipment.
Upgrade weapons.
Provide lore.
Offer optional quests.
Unlock hidden locations.
Become hostile depending on player decisions.
Die permanently if their questlines are neglected.
Include mysterious NPCs who appear across multiple regions.
8. MALGRAVEN AND THE MAIN STORY
Malgraven is an ancient wizard who summoned the protagonist from another dimension.
He discovered an ancient demon called THE DEVOURER BELOW, imprisoned beneath Eldoria by seven ancient kings.
The seals are failing.
Malgraven believes that someone from another dimension can destroy the demon because they are untouched by Eldoria's curse.
However, he secretly intends to sacrifice the protagonist during the final ritual.
The player must discover this betrayal through environmental storytelling, NPC dialogue, hidden documents, and boss encounters.
9. FINAL BOSS: THE DEVOURER BELOW
Create an enormous eldritch demon of unimaginable proportions.
Its body should contain embedded castles, twisted human faces, countless limbs, horns, and enormous masses of corrupted flesh.
The final encounter takes place across a collapsing kingdom.
PHASE ONE: THE AWAKENING
Fight the demon's gigantic limbs while traversing collapsing ruins.
PHASE TWO: THE GOD BENEATH
Enter the demon's body and fight the corrupted souls of the seven ancient kings.
PHASE THREE: THE UNHOLY TRUTH
Confront the demon's true form in an enormous supernatural arena.
Reality fractures, gravity changes, and the environment continuously transforms.
The final battle should feel overwhelming and cinematic while remaining mechanically fair and playable.
10. ENDINGS
Implement three possible endings based on player decisions and hidden quest requirements.
ENDING A: A NEW DAWN
The protagonist destroys the demon and saves Eldoria. A portal opens, allowing them to return to modern-day Earth.
ENDING B: THE HOLLOW CROWN
The protagonist absorbs the demon's remaining power and becomes Eldoria's new ruler, gradually transforming into an entity similar to the one they destroyed.
ENDING C: BEYOND THE VEIL
The protagonist discovers a hidden truth about Malgraven, the seven kings, and the origin of the demon. They reject both the wizard's ritual and the demon's influence, escaping into an unknown dimension.
11. GRAPHICS AND AUDIO
Use high-quality 3D graphics with:
Realistic character models.
Detailed armor and weapons.
Atmospheric lighting.
Volumetric fog.
Dynamic weather.
Realistic shadows.
High-quality environmental textures.
Destructible environmental elements where practical.
Detailed boss animations.
Visual direction should combine whimsical fairytale fantasy with disturbing gothic horror.
The world should feel beautiful from a distance but increasingly disturbing as the player explores.
Audio:
Orchestral dark fantasy soundtrack.
Gothic choir music.
Atmospheric environmental sounds.
Distinctive enemy vocalizations.
Heavy cinematic boss music.
Immersive weapon and combat sounds.
12. SAVE SYSTEM AND GAMEPLAY INTERFACE
Implement:
Checkpoint shrines.
Respawn mechanics.
Enemy respawning.
Currency loss upon death.
Currency recovery by returning to the death location.
Inventory.
Equipment menus.
Character statistics.
Quest tracking.
Map.
Boss health bars.
Dialogue interface.
Save and load functionality.
13. DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENTS
Generate this as an actual playable 3D game.
Do not generate only concept art, cinematic sequences, or static environments.
Build working gameplay systems, functional player controls, enemy AI, combat, progression, NPC interaction, and boss encounters.
Prioritize a polished playable vertical slice before attempting to generate the entire campaign.
The initial playable build must contain:
A complete opening cinematic.
The dimensional transportation sequence.
The first explorable region.
At least five ordinary enemy types.
One elite enemy.
One fully functional major boss: THE HOLLOW WOODSMAN.
A working checkpoint system.
A functional inventory and weapon system.
A basic progression system.
A clear objective leading to the next region.
Use modular, reusable game systems so additional regions, enemies, weapons, quests, and bosses can be added without rebuilding the entire project.
FINAL CREATIVE DIRECTION:
THE HOLLOW CROWN should feel like entering a beautiful children's fairytale that slowly reveals itself to be an enormous nightmare.
The player should constantly wonder what is around the next corner.
Make exploration rewarding, combat challenging, bosses terrifying, and the story mysterious.
Every region should feel like an entirely different world while remaining part of one interconnected kingdom.
Create an unforgettable Soulslike adventure where an ordinary human becomes the last hope of an entire dimension.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]

    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@07ad554e65d48f0aaa8780ec9fe681753cbd2fe4
    with:

    needs: prepare

    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write

So the runtime supports vite projects. We need to build a functioning 3D game using Three.js. This is a huge request; we need to create a polished vertical slice with the listed content. We have limited time/context, but can create a solid game.

Plan:
- Vite + Three.js app.
- Procedural low-poly/stylized 3D dark fantasy world (no external assets; use generated geometry, canvas textures, procedural audio). Maybe use three via npm.
- We can leverage Three.js only. No GLB assets likely. We can build characters from primitives with stylized shapes and animations via code (boneless but articulated groups). Should look reasonably good.
- Game architecture modular: engine, world, player, enemies, combat, bosses, UI, audio, save.
- Opening cinematic: dimension transport sequence via animated camera/scene overlay.
- Region 1: Forgotten Shire, with 5 enemy types, elite, boss Hollow Woodsman, checkpoint shrines, inventory/weapon system, progression, objective to next region.
- Also include six region stubs? Requirement says vertical slice: first region plus clear objective to next region. But genre description asks six regions. Prioritize vertical slice. Could implement all six as explorable "regions" with boss stubs? That's a lot. Maybe build region 1 fully and gate other regions in map as "coming"? Better to include selectable region portals with simpler generated regions and bosses? Time constraints. Focus on quality of vertical slice plus endings (three endings) maybe as narrative choices after final boss impossible. Hmm.

We need to decide scope realistically. The task explicitly says initial playable build must contain certain things. We'll deliver those. Include also a progression path and maybe post-boss unlock "Region 2 gate" objective, plus ending selection? Could add an ending hall after boss? Better maybe implement a boss victory cinematic and "To be continued" with endings? But the request asks three endings; initial build doesn't require. However, we can add ending choice via a final "vision" after the Hollow Woodsman? Not thematically fitting. Could include as meta: after boss, a "crown fragment" offers three choices (the three endings) — nice and demonstrates endings. But vertical slice story should lead to next region. Maybe implement an epilogue teaser and endings unlock as NG+? Hmm.

Let's focus: robust 3D Soulslike in one page, with plenty of systems. We can make the whole game set in the Forgotten Shire, with the boss, and after victory a portal to the Weeping Wilds. We can also include a compact "finale" playable sequence for the Devourer Below? That's beyond scope. We'll note assumptions: vertical slice.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable third-person 3D Soulslike action RPG titled **THE HOLLOW CROWN** in the blank `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround` repo, based on the detailed dark-fantasy design prompt.
- Deliver at minimum a polished vertical slice: opening cinematic, dimensional transport, Region 1 (The Forgotten Shire), 5+ enemy types, 1 elite, Hollow Woodsman boss, shrines, inventory/weapons, progression, and clear objective to Region 2.

## Requirements
- Browser-playable 3D game; must build/run via Vite and be captured with Playwright/WebGL.
- Keyboard + mouse and controller support.
- Soulslike combat: light/heavy attacks, dodge/roll, lock-on, block/parry, stamina, poise/stagger, backstab, criticals, healing, death/respawn.
- Six-region campaign concept, but prioritize a polished vertical slice first.
- Visual direction: whimsical fairytale gradually revealing gothic horror; high-quality procedural 3D, atmospheric lighting/fog, detailed bosses.
- Audio: orchestral/choir-like dark fantasy soundtrack, ambience, combat SFX.
- Systems: checkpoints, enemy respawn, currency loss/recovery, inventory, equipment, stats, quests, map, boss bar, dialogue, save/load.
- Three endings: A New Dawn, The Hollow Crown, Beyond the Veil.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them at the end.
- Do not generate only concept art/cinematics/static environments — actual gameplay required.

## Decisions
- Use **Three.js + Vite** with wholly procedural geometry, textures, animation, and WebAudio; no external assets.
- Deliver Region 1 as the polished vertical slice, plus a Chapter I completion gate, Seer’s Echo, and three ending previews. Regions II–VI are narrative/UI stubs only.
- Build procedural modular systems for terrain, props, enemies, bosses, combat, UI, and save so future regions can be added.
- Use stylized articulated primitive characters with procedural animation rather than GLB assets.
- Implement WebGL renderer (SwiftShader-compatible), no postprocessing, no shadow maps, blob shadows, merged/instanced scenery for performance.
- Save via `localStorage` (`hollow_crown_save_v1`).

## Work State

### Completed
- Created `package.json` with `three@^0.169.0`, `vite@^5.4.8`; ran `npm install`.
- Wrote `index.html`, `src/style.css`, and all major game modules:
  - `src/core/utils.js`, `input.js`, `audio.js`, `save.js`
  - `src/game/data.js`, `game.js`, `effects.js`, `intro.js`
  - `src/world/terrain.js`, `scenery.js`, `region1.js`
  - `src/entities/player.js`, `enemy.js`, `boss.js`, `npc.js`
  - `src/ui/ui.js`
- Implemented:
  - Procedural terrain, path, village, hollow tree, forest mushrooms, flowers, trees, rocks, shrines, boss arena, fog gate, lore pages, chests, motes, locket quest item, Seer’s Echo.
  - Player movement/sprint/jump/roll/lock-on/light-heavy attacks/block/parry/heal/spell/weapon swap/critical/death.
  - Enemy AI (patrol/detect/chase/attack/stagger/return), 5 ordinary types + elite Briar Warden, projectile archers.
  - Hollow Woodsman boss with 2 phases, sweep/slam/charge/root/summon attacks, intro, stagger, death.
  - NPC Marrow (shop/quests), Wisp (lore/truth), Seer’s Echo (three endings).
  - HUD, boss/elite bars, damage floats, toasts, pause/inventory/level-up/shop/map/lore/dialogue/controls/endings UI.
  - Opening rainy-city cinematic with rift and transport.
  - Save/load, shrine rest/respawn, currency bloodstain recovery, enemy respawn, three ending screens.
- `src/game/game.js` was just written but has not yet been linted/run in the browser.

### Active
- First integration/build/test pass is not yet done.
- Need to add missing CSS for `.float-text` and possibly `.menu-frame.wide`, and verify module import/runtime errors.
- Need to run `npm run build`/start server and use Playwright screenshot capture.
- Need to visually inspect title screen, cinematic, Region 1, combat, boss, menus; fix bugs and performance.

### Blocked
- No known blockers yet, but likely runtime errors from untested code and missing imports/API mismatches.

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` (or `npx vite build --base ./`) and fix syntax/import errors.
2. Add missing CSS classes (`.float-text`, `.menu-frame.wide`, disabled buttons, map sizing, ending screen).
3. Start server with `npm run dev`/`start.sh` on port 3002 and open via `playwright-cli`.
4. Verify title, start intro, skip intro, gameplay, shrine, enemy combat, boss intro/fight, death/respawn, inventory, shop, map, endings, save/continue.
5. Capture and inspect screenshots; fix visual defects (camera, models, lighting, clipping, UI).
6. Check gamepad mappings and pointer lock; ensure all input actions work.
7. Run a final full playthrough via automation, fix regressions, and note assumptions/scope in the final response.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/game.js`: central orchestration; just written, untested.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/entities/player.js`: player movement/combat/animation; core gameplay.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/entities/enemy.js`: enemy AI/models; likely integration issues.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world/region1.js`: world composition, spawns, interactables.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world/scenery.js`: large procedural environment; likely visual/perf tuning.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world/terrain.js`: terrain height, path, arena definition.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/intro.js`: opening cinematic scene.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/save.js`: save schema; may need `openedChests`, `collectedMotes`, `xp`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM IDs referenced by UI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: UI styling; missing `.float-text` CSS.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Vite/Three scripts and dependencies.

## Important Context
- Environment uses `RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime`; `start.sh` runs `default-start.mjs`, which supports Vite, builds to `dist`, serves on `PORT` (likely 3002).
- Use `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`; Chromium uses SwiftShader CPU rendering, not hardware GPU. Screenshot output should go to `screenshots/`.
- `src/game/game.js` references `this.world.interactables`, `this.world.motes`, `this.world.locket`, `this.world.echo`, `this.world.gate`, `this.world.shrines`, `this.world.chests`, `this.world.spawns`, `this.world.npcSpots`, all produced by `buildRegion`.
- `save.js` currently lacks `openedChests`, `collectedMotes`, `xp` in `defaultState`, although `game.js` reads/writes them; add them.
- `game.js` calls `this.ui.showLore(...)`; UI has `showLore`, but `openLoreUI` manually re-assigns `currentMenu`; verify menu close behavior.
- `game.js` calls `this.ui.updateFloatTexts(raw)` and `this.ui.updateVitals`, etc.; UI implements these.
- Potential runtime bug: `Player.update()` reads movement input even when `uiBlocking` is true; Game skips player update while blocked, so mostly safe.
- Potential runtime bug: `game.js` `updateInteract()` may call `this.input.consumePressed` while Input has already ended frame—only called before `endFrame`, okay.
- Potential runtime bug: `Enemy.updateFlash()` resets emissive on all `mats` every frame, possibly overriding intended materials; visually inspect.
- Potential runtime bug: `NPC.dialogue()` Wisp branch references `s.lore.length`; state always has lore array.
- Potential runtime bug: title attract camera uses `this.player.animate(raw)` but player not positioned under tree; acceptable.
- Need to ensure `startNewGame` and `continueGame` call audio init after user gesture (they do via button click).
- `src/game/game.js` `saveGame()` adds `playtime` and then `returnToTitle()` calls `saveGame()` again; may double-count playtime; check.
- `src/game/game.js` `openEndings()` calls `closeDialogueSilently()` then shows menu; closing dialogue doesn’t reset `uiBlocking`, but `openEndings` sets it true.
- `src/game/game.js` `chooseEnding()` sets mode `'ending'`, calls `saveGame()` while mode is already `'ending'`—saveGame only skips intro, so fine.
- Need to verify whether `--base ./` build works with `main.js` absolute import `/src/main.js`; Vite handles it, but static server output should be tested.
- The final response should note assumptions/scope: vertical slice only for Regions II–VI, procedural visuals/audio, three endings presented as Seer’s Echo vision, no external assets.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable third-person 3D Soulslike action RPG titled **THE HOLLOW CROWN** in the blank `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround` repo, based on a detailed dark-fantasy design prompt.
- Deliver a polished vertical slice: opening cinematic, dimensional transport, Region 1 (The Forgotten Shire), 5+ enemy types, 1 elite, Hollow Woodsman boss, shrines, inventory/weapons, progression, and clear objective to Region 2.

## Requirements
- Browser-playable 3D game; must build/run via Vite and be captured with Playwright/WebGL.
- Keyboard + mouse and controller support.
- Soulslike combat: light/heavy attacks, dodge/roll, lock-on, block/parry, stamina, poise/stagger, backstab, criticals, healing, death/respawn.
- Six-region campaign concept, but prioritize a polished vertical slice first.
- Visual direction: whimsical fairytale gradually revealing gothic horror; high-quality procedural 3D, atmospheric lighting/fog, detailed bosses.
- Audio: orchestral/choir-like dark fantasy soundtrack, ambience, combat SFX.
- Systems: checkpoints, enemy respawn, currency loss/recovery, inventory, equipment, stats, quests, map, boss bar, dialogue, save/load.
- Three endings: A New Dawn, The Hollow Crown, Beyond the Veil.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them at the end.
- Do not generate only concept art/cinematics/static environments — actual gameplay required.

## Decisions
- Use **Three.js + Vite** with wholly procedural geometry, textures, animation, and WebAudio; no external assets.
- Deliver Region 1 as the polished vertical slice, plus a Chapter I completion gate, Seer’s Echo, and three ending previews. Regions II–VI are narrative/UI stubs only.
- Build procedural modular systems for terrain, props, enemies, bosses, combat, UI, and save so future regions can be added.
- Use stylized articulated primitive characters with procedural animation rather than GLB assets.
- Implement WebGL renderer (SwiftShader-compatible), no postprocessing, no shadow maps, blob shadows, merged/instanced scenery for performance.
- Save via `localStorage` (`hollow_crown_save_v1`).

## Work State

### Completed
- Created `package.json` with `three@^0.169.0`, `vite@^5.4.8`; installed dependencies.
- Wrote `index.html`, `src/style.css`, and all major game modules:
  - `src/core/utils.js`, `input.js`, `audio.js`, `save.js`
  - `src/game/data.js`, `game.js`, `effects.js`, `intro.js`
  - `src/world/terrain.js`, `scenery.js`, `region1.js`
  - `src/entities/player.js`, `enemy.js`, `boss.js`, `npc.js`
  - `src/ui/ui.js`
- Implemented procedural terrain, path, village, hollow tree, forest mushrooms, flowers, trees, rocks, shrines, boss arena, fog gate, lore pages, chests, motes, locket quest item, Seer’s Echo.
- Implemented player movement/sprint/jump/roll/lock-on/light-heavy attacks/block/parry/heal/spell/weapon swap/critical/death.
- Implemented enemy AI (patrol/detect/chase/attack/stagger/return), 5 ordinary types + elite Briar Warden, projectile archers.
- Implemented Hollow Woodsman boss with 2 phases, sweep/slam/charge/root/summon attacks, intro, stagger, death.
- Implemented NPC Marrow (shop/quests), Wisp (lore/truth), Seer’s Echo (three endings).
- Implemented HUD, boss/elite bars, damage floats, toasts, pause/inventory/level-up/shop/map/lore/dialogue/controls/endings UI.
- Implemented opening rainy-city cinematic with rift and transport.
- Implemented save/load, shrine rest/respawn, currency bloodstain recovery, enemy respawn, three ending screens.
- Added missing `src/main.js` bootstrap; fixed build failure from missing entry point.
- `npm run build` now succeeds (`dist` generated; ~705 kB JS, expected chunk-size warning).
- Added missing `.float-text` CSS classes for combat/reward text.
- Added missing UI element IDs (`flask-icon`, `buff-icons`, `gamepad-hint`) and fixed `UI.updateVitals()` null lookup.
- Fixed `Game.startNewGame()` fade so the opening cinematic is visible immediately instead of black for ~20 seconds.
- Fixed `createBossArena()` return to include `ring2`, resolving title-scene runtime errors.
- Fixed quadruped enemy `alertIcon`/`telegraph` creation by ensuring `addTelegraph()` and `addAlertIcon()` run for all enemy models.
- Fixed `Player.beginRoll()` using `game.camera.yaw` instead of `game.cameraRig.yaw`.
- Added `openedChests`, `collectedMotes`, and `xp` to `defaultState()`.
- Added NPC `onOpen` callback execution in `UI.openDialogue()`.
- Playwright Chromium installed and successfully opened via `playwright-cli`.
- Captured and visually inspected: title screen, opening rain cinematic, first gameplay view, pause menu.
- Movement verified via direct input: player position changes and `state='move'`.
- Intro lighting improved (brighter ambient, directional, street and neon lights; less dense fog).

### Active
- Full integration/playtest pass is in progress.
- Need to run `/tmp/opencode/verify.mjs` to automate intro, gameplay, combat, menus, boss intro/fight/death, chapter end, and endings with screenshot capture.
- Need to inspect resulting screenshots and fix visual/runtime defects.
- Need to verify all enemy types, elite encounter, quest, shop, level-up, map, lore, save/continue, death/respawn, and gamepad/pointer-lock behavior.

### Blocked
- No known hard blockers; runtime errors so far have been fixed.

## Next Move
1. Run `node /tmp/opencode/verify.mjs` (server on port `3002`, Playwright already installed) and inspect all generated screenshots in `screenshots/`.
2. Fix any page/runtime errors surfaced by the script, especially combat, boss, menus, and endings.
3. Test and tune combat feel: enemy aggro, hit detection, lock-on camera, boss telegraphs, player damage/stamina, critical/backstab.
4. Test UI flows end-to-end: shrine rest/save, level-up, shop, inventory/equip, map, lore overlay, dialogue, chapter-end gate, all three endings.
5. Test save/continue, death/respawn, bloodstain recovery, chests, motes, quest item, and Seer’s Echo.
6. Inspect and improve title framing, HUD contrast on bright backgrounds, intro visibility/impact, and boss arena readability.
7. Verify controller mappings and pointer-lock behavior; run final production build.
8. Note assumptions/scope in final response: Regions II–VI are stubs, all art/audio procedural, endings presented via Seer’s Echo.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/entities/player.js`: player movement/combat/animation; recent roll-camera fix.

- `src/game/game.js` reads `this.world.interactables`, `motes`, `locket`, `echo`, `gate`, `shrines`, `chests`, `spawns`, `npcSpots`, `colliders`; all provided by `buildRegion`.
- Runtime error already fixed: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rotation')` at `region1.js` due missing `arena.ring2`.
- Runtime error already fixed: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'visible')` at `enemy.js` due missing `alertIcon` on hounds.

Now we understand. We need to add Xbox controller support robustly:

1. Improve Input class:
   - Detect gamepad type / mapping (standard).
   - Proper deadzones with radial scaling, independent axes, handle axes for controllers where axes[2]/[3] may be triggers instead (some non-standard). Xbox standard mapping is fine.
   - Button mapping: track press/release, add support for D-pad nav (GP12-15), shoulder/trigger. Fix conflicts: current jump GP0 conflicts with confirm/critical; map critical maybe not critical button? Let's inspect player.js usage of input actions, especially critical. Also check UI needs.
   - Add semantic actions: menuUp/menuDown/menuLeft/menuRight (D-pad + left stick repeat), menuConfirm (A), menuCancel (B), pause/start.
   - Sprint: hold B (GP1) while moving maybe, but roll on B press. Typical souls: B dodge on tap, hold to sprint. But player likely uses input.dodge separately, and sprintHeld getter. Could include `walk` on LS. Let's map sprintHeld = Shift or LS click or RB? Current GP10 LS click. Add GP1 held as sprint? That could conflict because dodge triggers on press, sprint on hold; player.beginRoll on press then sprint. Actually if B pressed triggers dodge and holding triggers sprint, sprint after roll may be okay. But better use LS click (GP10) and/or RB (GP5) held? RB used for dodge currently incorrectly. Typical Xbox soulslike: RB = light attack, RT = heavy attack, LB = block, LT = parry? Actually in many games: RB light, RT heavy, LB block, LT parry, B dodge, A interact, Y lock, X heal, D-pad weapon, Start pause, View inventory.
   
   Current: light RT (GP7), heavy LT (GP6), block LB (GP4), dodge B (GP1) and RB (GP5), jump A (GP0), sprint LS (GP10), lock Y (GP3), interact X (GP2), heal D-pad down (GP13), spell D-pad up (GP12), inventory View (GP8), map A (GP0 conflict), pause Menu (GP9), weapon next D-pad right/Sprint.

   Need rational mapping. I'd propose:
   - A (0): interact / confirm; no jump, or jump remains? The game has jump (KeyF). Third-person soulslike doesn't need jump much, but could map jump to LS click. Hmm.
   - B (1): dodge/roll; hold to sprint.
   - X (2): heal (flask) — typical Souls X/Square heal.
   - Y (3): lock-on.
   - LB (4): block (hold).
   - RB (5): light attack.
   - LT (6): heavy attack? But analog triggers act as buttons. Some controllers only report value, not pressed. We map value > 0.5, good.
   - RT (7): heavy attack or light? Common: RB light, RT heavy, LB block, LT parry. Use RB light, RT heavy, LB block, LT block/parry? Block is hold, parry maybe timed block? Let's inspect player.blockHeld and parry logic. Search.
   - D-pad up (12): spell

   - D-pad left/right (14/15): weapon prev/next

   - Implement a `UI` gamepad navigation that runs every frame even when input is processed. It can use `input.wasPressed('GP12')`, `GP13`, `GP14`, `GP15` and left-stick directional repeat, and `GP0`/`GP1` confirm/cancel.

Add visual style `:focus` / `.gp-focus`.
   - For dialogue, up/down cycles options, A selects.

But UI update in menu mode is called, with input state. We can process there.
   - Need avoid A being used for gameplay interact when menu opened same frame? The menus are opened via E, not A (interact is X). Good, but `input.confirm` currently includes GP0; game loop uiBlocking checks `input.confirm` to close menu when ui currentMenu. That would instantly close any menu opened by an A press? A is not interact anymore, but if A opens menu somehow? It doesn't. Current code: if (uiBlocking) { if (currentMenu && (pause||confirm)) { if (pause) closeMenu(); } ... }—confirm does nothing there except condition, only pause closes. So fine. But we should remove weird confirm condition maybe.

   - For dialogue, A = select focused/first, B = close, D-pad = cycle.
   - Add prompts in UI text to reflect controller: dialogue hint "[A] choose · [B] leave · D-pad select" etc. Maybe dynamic based on last input type. Implement `input.lastDevice` 'gamepad' or 'keyboard'. Then UI can update hints. HUD interact prompt currently shows `.key` as "E"; update to "A" when gamepad used. Similarly pause footer etc. Might be substantial but doable.

4. Fix camera look: right stick axes mapping, invert Y, sensitivity settings. Current `rig.pitch += lookY * dt * 1.6` (stick down increases pitch => camera higher? maybe inverted). Standard: right stick up look up (decrease pitch? rig.pitch is elevation; increasing pitch raises camera and looks down. So stick up should lower pitch. Current positive lookY (stick down) increases pitch => camera up/look down; that's non-inverted? In typical third-person, pushing right stick up should move camera up and look down? Actually most games: push right stick up looks up. Camera pitch increases upward direction. Here rig.pitch is camera elevation above target; increasing pitch raises camera, causing look down at player but view direction downward. So to look up, lower camera pitch? Wait the camera is behind and above player. If pitch increases, camera y increases, camera looks at player, so view tilts downward. So pushing stick down => look down; pushing up => look up. Current `rig.pitch += lookY * dt * 1.6` with lookY = stick down positive => pitch increases => look down. That's correct (non-inverted). For mouse, moving mouse down increases mouseDY positive => pitch increases => look down. Correct. Fine.

   Right stick yaw: pushing right => lookX positive => rig.yaw -= positive => camera rotates right? `off = (sin yaw, cos yaw)`, camera behind based on yaw. Player moves relative to camera yaw. Decreasing yaw rotates camera... Let's see, at yaw=0 camera offset +z (behind +z), looking toward -z. yaw negative -> camera offset x negative, z positive => camera moves to left, looks toward right, so view rotates right. Yes pushing right looks right. Good.

   Need smooth deadzone response and maybe swap axis mapping if standard mapping and axes[2]/[3] are triggers? On Xbox controller standard mapping axes: 0 left X, 1 left Y, 2 right X, 3 right Y. Good.

5. Handle gamepadconnect hints: UI currently has gamepad-hint element, but never shown? Search for gpadchange usage. Only input dispatch, no listeners. Add UI listener to show hint; hide after 3.5s. Also maybe show in title. Good.

6. Add controller diagram / controls list entries. Data.js CONTROLS currently keyboard only. Add controller section or update entries with Xbox buttons. Let's inspect data.js CONTROLS.

"Genre: 3D Soulslike Action RPG / Dark Fantasy / Open-World Exploration
Perspective: Third-person
Visual Style: High-quality 3D dark fantasy with whimsical fairytale environments
Combat Inspiration: Dark Souls, Elden Ring, Lies of P
Platform: PC (controller and keyboard support)
1. GAME OVERVIEW
Create a fully playable third-person 3D Soulslike action RPG titled THE HOLLOW CROWN.
The player is an ordinary modern-day human who is mysteriously transported from 2026 into a whimsical medieval fantasy kingdom called Eldoria.
The kingdom initially appears colorful, magical, and fairytale-like, filled with enchanted forests, talking creatures, enormous mushrooms, medieval villages, castles, and magical landscapes.
However, a terrible corruption has spread throughout the kingdom. Villagers have transformed into hostile creatures, knights have become undead monsters, and ancient supernatural entities are awakening.
The player's ultimate objective is to fight through six interconnected regions, defeat powerful bosses, uncover the kingdom's secrets, and confront an ancient eldritch wizard responsible for bringing them into this world.
Eventually, the player must face an enormous unholy demon threatening to consume all of existence.
2. PLAYER CHARACTER
Create a customizable human protagonist.
The character begins wearing recognizable modern clothing, including a hoodie, pants, and sneakers.
Starting equipment:
Broken smartphone (nonfunctional).
Improvised metal pipe.
Basic healing item.
No armor.
No magical abilities.
The character must gradually evolve from an ordinary human into a powerful warrior.
Implement:
Character movement.
Sprinting.
Jumping.
Dodging and rolling.
Lock-on targeting.
Light and heavy attacks.
Blocking and parrying.
Stamina management.
Health management.
Weapon switching.
Armor equipment.
Healing animations.
Death and respawn mechanics.
Include character progression through experience, currency, attributes, weapons, armor, and magical abilities.
3. CORE COMBAT SYSTEM
Implement challenging Soulslike combat.
Combat must be deliberate and weighty rather than fast-paced hack-and-slash.
Every weapon should have unique attack animations, damage values, stamina consumption, and attack ranges.
Weapon categories:
Straight swords.
Greatswords.
Daggers.
Axes.
Warhammers.
Spears.
Bows.
Magical staffs.
Unique boss weapons.
Combat mechanics:
Enemy telegraph animations.
Perfect dodge timing.
Parrying and critical attacks.
Stagger and poise systems.
Backstab attacks.
Critical finishing animations.
Boss health bars.
Multiple boss phases.
Environmental hazards.
Enemies must be dangerous enough that careless attacks can result in death.
4. WORLD DESIGN
Create six interconnected explorable regions with interconnected paths, shortcuts, hidden rooms, treasure, dungeons, NPCs, and boss arenas.
REGION 1: THE FORGOTTEN SHIRE
A whimsical medieval countryside filled with abandoned cottages, colorful flowers, enchanted hills, and corrupted villagers.
Enemies:
Infected villagers.
Glimmer goblins.
Hollow woodland creatures.
Rotten knights.
Main Boss: THE HOLLOW WOODSMAN.
A gigantic lumberjack with a massive axe and a tree growing through his chest.
REGION 2: THE WEEPING WILDS
A magical forest with enormous mushrooms, glowing plants, twisted trees, and underground fungal caverns.
Enemies:
Giant spiders.
Infected animals.
Mushroom creatures.
Root monsters.
Main Boss: MOTHER MYCELIA.
A grotesque mushroom queen who controls the forest through fungal roots.
REGION 3: THE KINGDOM OF ASHENVEIL
A sprawling medieval city with gothic cathedrals, burning streets, ruined marketplaces, and enormous castles.
Enemies:
Undead knights.
Executioners.
Plague doctors.
Corrupted royal guards.
Main Boss: KING ALDRIC, THE UNCROWNED.
A gigantic armored king wielding an enormous cursed sword.
REGION 4: THE FROSTBITTEN REACH
A frozen mountain kingdom containing abandoned fortresses, frozen lakes, ancient tombs, and blizzards.
Enemies:
Frozen warriors.
Ice giants.
Undead wolves.
Frost wraiths.
Main Boss: THE PALE SAINT.
A horrifying winged executioner inside a frozen cathedral.
REGION 5: THE SHATTERED HEAVENS
A surreal cosmic environment containing floating islands, broken castles, upside-down architecture, and strange celestial creatures.
Enemies:
Voidborn.
Floating aberrations.
Cosmic knights.
Distorted humanoids.
Main Boss: THE STARVED ORACLE.
A many-eyed celestial creature capable of manipulating gravity and creating illusions.
REGION 6: THE BLACK SPIRE
An enormous eldritch tower stretching into the heavens, surrounded by a seemingly endless void.
Enemies:
Malgraven's experiments.
Failed dimensional travelers.
Eldritch abominations.
Ancient corrupted guardians.
Main Boss: MALGRAVEN, THE LAST SEER.
The ancient wizard responsible for summoning the protagonist.
5. ENEMY AI
Create intelligent enemy behavior.
Enemies must:
Patrol designated areas.
Detect the player through vision and proximity.
Investigate suspicious sounds.
Pursue the player.
Attack using different patterns.
Retreat or reposition when appropriate.
Coordinate attacks in groups.
Return to patrol if the player escapes.
Each enemy type must have unique animations, movement, sounds, attack patterns, and visual designs.
Include rare elite enemies and hidden mini-boss encounters.
6. BOSS DESIGN
Every major boss must have:
Unique 3D character models.
Custom animations.
Distinctive music.
A dedicated arena.
Multiple combat phases.
Unique attack patterns.
Environmental interactions.
A cinematic introduction.
A dramatic death animation.
Unique rewards.
Boss difficulty should progressively increase throughout the campaign.
Bosses must not feel like oversized ordinary enemies. They should have recognizable personalities and memorable combat mechanics.
7. NPC AND QUEST SYSTEM
Populate Eldoria with survivors, merchants, mysterious travelers, talking creatures, and strange magical beings.
Create branching dialogue and questlines.
NPCs should remember important player decisions.
Some NPCs can:
Sell equipment.
Upgrade weapons.
Provide lore.
Offer optional quests.
Unlock hidden locations.
Become hostile depending on player decisions.
Die permanently if their questlines are neglected.
Include mysterious NPCs who appear across multiple regions.
8. MALGRAVEN AND THE MAIN STORY
Malgraven is an ancient wizard who summoned the protagonist from another dimension.
He discovered an ancient demon called THE DEVOURER BELOW, imprisoned beneath Eldoria by seven ancient kings.
The seals are failing.
Malgraven believes that someone from another dimension can destroy the demon because they are untouched by Eldoria's curse.
However, he secretly intends to sacrifice the protagonist during the final ritual.
The player must discover this betrayal through environmental storytelling, NPC dialogue, hidden documents, and boss encounters.
9. FINAL BOSS: THE DEVOURER BELOW
Create an enormous eldritch demon of unimaginable proportions.
Its body should contain embedded castles, twisted human faces, countless limbs, horns, and enormous masses of corrupted flesh.
The final encounter takes place across a collapsing kingdom.
PHASE ONE: THE AWAKENING
Fight the demon's gigantic limbs while traversing collapsing ruins.
PHASE TWO: THE GOD BENEATH
Enter the demon's body and fight the corrupted souls of the seven ancient kings.
PHASE THREE: THE UNHOLY TRUTH
Confront the demon's true form in an enormous supernatural arena.
Reality fractures, gravity changes, and the environment continuously transforms.
The final battle should feel overwhelming and cinematic while remaining mechanically fair and playable.
10. ENDINGS
Implement three possible endings based on player decisions and hidden quest requirements.
ENDING A: A NEW DAWN
The protagonist destroys the demon and saves Eldoria. A portal opens, allowing them to return to modern-day Earth.
ENDING B: THE HOLLOW CROWN
The protagonist absorbs the demon's remaining power and becomes Eldoria's new ruler, gradually transforming into an entity similar to the one they destroyed.
ENDING C: BEYOND THE VEIL
The protagonist discovers a hidden truth about Malgraven, the seven kings, and the origin of the demon. They reject both the wizard's ritual and the demon's influence, escaping into an unknown dimension.
11. GRAPHICS AND AUDIO
Use high-quality 3D graphics with:
Realistic character models.
Detailed armor and weapons.
Atmospheric lighting.
Volumetric fog.
Dynamic weather.
Realistic shadows.
High-quality environmental textures.
Destructible environmental elements where practical.
Detailed boss animations.
Visual direction should combine whimsical fairytale fantasy with disturbing gothic horror.
The world should feel beautiful from a distance but increasingly disturbing as the player explores.
Audio:
Orchestral dark fantasy soundtrack.
Gothic choir music.
Atmospheric environmental sounds.
Distinctive enemy vocalizations.
Heavy cinematic boss music.
Immersive weapon and combat sounds.
12. SAVE SYSTEM AND GAMEPLAY INTERFACE
Implement:
Checkpoint shrines.
Respawn mechanics.
Enemy respawning.
Currency loss upon death.
Currency recovery by returning to the death location.
Inventory.
Equipment menus.
Character statistics.
Quest tracking.
Map.
Boss health bars.
Dialogue interface.
Save and load functionality.
13. DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENTS
Generate this as an actual playable 3D game.
Do not generate only concept art, cinematic sequences, or static environments.
Build working gameplay systems, functional player controls, enemy AI, combat, progression, NPC interaction, and boss encounters.
Prioritize a polished playable vertical slice before attempting to generate the entire campaign.
The initial playable build must contain:
A complete opening cinematic.
The dimensional transportation sequence.
The first explorable region.
At least five ordinary enemy types.
One elite enemy.
One fully functional major boss: THE HOLLOW WOODSMAN.
A working checkpoint system.
A functional inventory and weapon system.
A basic progression system.
A clear objective leading to the next region.
Use modular, reusable game systems so additional regions, enemies, weapons, quests, and bosses can be added without rebuilding the entire project.
FINAL CREATIVE DIRECTION:
THE HOLLOW CROWN should feel like entering a beautiful children's fairytale that slowly reveals itself to be an enormous nightmare.
The player should constantly wonder what is around the next corner.
Make exploration rewarding, combat challenging, bosses terrifying, and the story mysterious.
Every region should feel like an entirely different world while remaining part of one interconnected kingdom.
Create an unforgettable Soulslike adventure where an ordinary human becomes the last hope of an entire dimension.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.
"
